case_name: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
summary: Established the basic structure doctrine limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution. The Court held that while Parliament has wide powers to amend the Constitution, it cannot alter its basic structure or framework including judicial review, federalism, and fundamental rights.

case_name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
summary: Expanded the interpretation of Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty) to include due process requirements. The Court held that any law depriving a person of personal liberty must be just, fair, and reasonable, establishing procedural safeguards.

case_name: Golaknath v. State of Punjab
summary: Held that Parliament cannot amend fundamental rights under Article 368. Though later overruled by Kesavananda, it introduced the doctrine of prospective overruling in India and emphasized the primacy of fundamental rights.

case_name: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India
summary: Reaffirmed the basic structure doctrine. Struck down clauses of the 42nd Amendment that sought to exclude judicial review of constitutional amendments and give primacy to Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights.

case_name: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
summary: Established guidelines for invoking President's Rule under Article 356 and declared secularism as part of the basic structure. Limited executive discretion in dismissing state governments and strengthened federal principles.

case_name: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
summary: Laid down comprehensive guidelines to prevent sexual harassment of women at workplaces. Relied on international conventions (CEDAW) to fill legislative vacuum until Parliament enacted the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013.

case_name: NALSA v. Union of India
summary: Recognized transgender persons as the 'third gender' and affirmed their fundamental rights under Articles 14, 15, 16, 19, and 21. Directed governments to provide reservations and welfare schemes for transgender community.

case_name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
summary: Decriminalized consensual homosexual acts between adults by reading down Section 377 IPC. Upheld the constitutional morality over social morality and recognized the right to sexuality as part of the right to privacy.

case_name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
summary: Declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21. Overruled earlier judgments and held that privacy includes informational privacy, physical privacy, and decisional autonomy.

case_name: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
summary: Laid down 11 mandatory guidelines to prevent custodial violence and torture. Mandated procedures for arrest including informing relatives, medical examination, and maintaining arrest memo. Cornerstone for protecting rights of arrested persons.

case_name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
summary: Restricted automatic arrests under Section 498A IPC (matrimonial cruelty). Directed police to follow checklist before arrest in cases punishable up to 7 years. Magistrates must record reasons for authorizing detention.

case_name: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P.
summary: Held that registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence. Police cannot conduct preliminary inquiry before registering FIR in such cases.

case_name: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
summary: Held that divorced Muslim women are entitled to maintenance under Section 125 CrPC. Advocated for a Uniform Civil Code. Led to significant debate on personal laws and parliamentary response through Muslim Women Act 1986.

case_name: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
summary: Declared instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) unconstitutional and void. Held that arbitrary and unilateral divorce violates Article 14 (equality). Led to enactment of Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak)
summary: Evolved the doctrine of 'absolute liability' for hazardous industries, going beyond the English rule in Rylands v. Fletcher. Enterprises engaged in inherently dangerous activities are absolutely liable for harm, with no exceptions.

case_name: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
summary: Incorporated 'precautionary principle' and 'polluter pays principle' as part of environmental law in India. Held that sustainable development is essential for environmental protection and imposed liability on polluting industries.

case_name: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
summary: Upheld 27% reservation for OBCs but introduced 'creamy layer' exclusion. Set 50% ceiling on total reservations. Held that economic criteria alone cannot be basis for reservation; social and educational backwardness is essential.

case_name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
summary: Struck down Section 66A of IT Act as unconstitutional for being vague and having chilling effect on free speech. Distinguished between 'discussion', 'advocacy', and 'incitement'. Landmark for digital rights in India.

case_name: Common Cause v. Union of India (Euthanasia)
summary: Legalized passive euthanasia and recognized the validity of 'living wills' or advance medical directives. Held that the right to die with dignity is part of Article 21. Laid down guidelines for passive euthanasia.

case_name: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
summary: Struck down Section 497 IPC (adultery) as unconstitutional. Held that the law was based on patriarchal notions treating women as property of husbands. Decriminalized adultery while noting it remains a ground for divorce.
